builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
summary: Replaces manual expert-driven cycles of model selection, hyperparameter tuning, data curation, and per-device quantization testing with an orchestrator-LLM-driven search that uses real on-device measurements and rule-based rollback. Costs include orchestrator LLM API calls, GPU time for fine-tuning candidates, phone-specific measurement infrastructure across inference engines, and integration complexity of the agentic pipeline. The method can fail on tasks outside the ten evaluated, the adaptive accuracy goal may settle below achievable quality, and results depend on access to target phones, so conclusions may not transfer to devices or engines not measured.
rationale: The approach is relevant to shipping private on-device models on a limited budget, but its gains are validated on only ten tasks and four phones, so workload-specific validation on the reader's own task and target device is required before adoption.
technique: Agentic SLM selection and fine-tuning factory for on-device deployment

claims.statement: Replaces manual expert-driven cycles of model selection, hyperparameter tuning, data curation, and per-device quantization testing with an orchestrator-LLM-driven search that uses real on-device measurements and rule-based rollback. Costs include orchestrator LLM API calls, GPU time for fine-tuning candidates, phone-specific measurement infrastructure across inference engines, and integration complexity of the agentic pipeline. The method can fail on tasks outside the ten evaluated, the adaptive accuracy goal may settle below achievable quality, and results depend on access to target phones, so conclusions may not transfer to devices or engines not measured.

Search comes within 0.03 accuracy of exhaustively training all 27 model variants on an entity extraction task while using 19x less GPU time; on-device models outperform two five-shot frontier models on five of ten tasks (by up to 0.34) and match on three more.
